Under this section it has been held that for causing grievous hurt to a woman by her husband or his relatives or anyone on his behalf over the demand of dowry would be an offence under section 11. In order to convict under this section, the prosecution has to prove two things: whether the victim was caused grievous hurt and that grievous hurt was caused for nonpayment of dowry. 

 38. Now let us turn to the point as regards the joint trial of scheduled and non scheduled offence. It appears from evidence on record that the accused Abdul Kader was convicted under section 11 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Bishesh Bidhan Ain, 1995 and section 306 of the Penal Code. The offence under section 11 is a scheduled offence triable by Special Tribunal like Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Bishesh Bidhan Adalat whereas the offence under section 306 of the Penal Code is a non scheduled offence triable by General Criminal Court. Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Bishesh Bidhan Adalat has no jurisdiction to try the offence under section 306 of the Penal Code. 

 39. Joinder of scheduled offence and nonscheduled offence in framing charge is illegal and trial on such a charge is without jurisdiction. Taking of cognisance of scheduled and non-scheduled offence, the framing of charge thereof and the trial upon charges in both the scheduled and nonscheduled offence together suffered from a complete lack of jurisdiction and conviction there under vitiates the whole proceedings and conviction is liable to be set aside. We find support of the above view in the case of Mozammel Hoque vs State reported in 43 DLR 614. Here in this case we find that the learned Judge Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Bishesh Bidhan Adalat has committed gross illegality by taking scheduled offence and nonscheduled offence together for trial which vitiates the trial as a whole.
